Junkoo Kim, Founder and CEO, said, “We delivered third quarter reported revenue and Adjusted EBITDA within our guidance ranges while continuing to invest with discipline in our next phase of growth, and we are confident in our return to double-digit revenue growth in the fourth quarter.” Kim continued, “Our strategy is working across the business. On-platform, we are strengthening how readers discover and engage with stories; Off-platform, we are turning our IP into global franchises across diverse formats; and through collaborations, we are extending our reach to new audiences. Each reinforces the other, and together they position us for durable, long-term growth. This is the future of storytelling, and WEBTOON is building it.” Fourth Quarter 2026 Outlook For the fourth quarter 2026, the Company expects: • Revenue growth on a constant currency basis in the range of 9.0%-12.0%. This represents revenue in the range of $371-$381 million, based on current FX rates. • Adjusted EBITDA in the range of $0.0-$5.0 million, representing an Adjusted EBITDA Margin in the range of 0.0%-1.3%. Our fourth quarter 2026 outlook includes expected revenue and contributions from RI Games Holdings

The risk-benefit profile of thrombolytic therapy in minor stroke patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) remains uncertain. This post hoc analysis of the TRUST trial (ThRombolysis with Urokinase for minor Stroke Trial) sought to comparatively assess whether the presence of large vessel occlusion (LVO) modifies the efficacy and safety of urokinase intravenous thrombolysis, compared with best medical treatment(BMT), in patients with minor stroke. This post-hoc exploratory analysis included patients from the TRUST trial with available vascular imaging data, categorized in the LVO and the non-LVO group. Each group was further divided into the UK thrombolysis group and the BMT group. Primary efficacy outcome was the proportion of patients achieving a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-1 at 90 days. Postoperative infections are a leading cause of maternal morbidity after emergency cesarean delivery. This trial explores the effectiveness of preoperative vaginal cleansing via the use of chlorhexidine for reducing these complications in women in labor. This single-blinded superiority randomized controlled trial included 840 women in labor equally distributed to either immediate preoperative chlorhexidine gluconate 0.05% vaginal cleansing or no-cleansing; 826 were analyzed under a modified intention-to-treat approach. The co-primary outcomes were postcesarean endometritis and surgical site infection (SSI). Secondary outcomes included composite wound complications, postoperative fever, significant leukocytosis, hospital readmission, length of stay, and adverse drug reactions. Effects are expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals, with adjusted, sensitivity, and subgroup analyses for the co-primary outcomes. Chlorhexidine significantly reduced both co-primary outcomes; postcesarean endometritis (1.9% vs. 6.3%; RR 0.303, 95% CI 0.139-0.662; P = 0.001) and SSI (1.4% vs. 5.4%; RR 0.269, 95% CI 0.110-0.656; P = 0.002); both remained significant against a Bonferroni-adjusted threshold of 0.025. Other outcomes were also reduced, including composite wound complications (3.4% vs. 11.0%; RR 0.307, 95% CI 0.171-0.550; P < 0.001), and readmission for infection (1.4% vs. 6.3%; P < 0.001; RR 0.227, 95% CI 0.095-0.547). The co-primary outcome effects persisted after adjustment and in sensitivity analyses. Treatment effects were in the same direction across premature rupture of membranes (PROM) and obesity subgroups with no significant interaction, although the SSI reduction reached significance overall and in the non-obese stratum but not within the obese stratum. As a low-cost intervention that can be integrated into existing perioperative workflows, it is a promising strategy for reducing maternal infection; however, adverse events were not systematically solicited, and neonatal exposure was not assessed. Multicenter confirmation, systematic maternal and neonatal safety data, and cost-effectiveness analysis are required before routine adoption.
